Sam Rivera: Quick check — about to push a Terraform change for the inference-gateway k8s Service to enable NLB passthrough (NodePort). Want to confirm healthcheck behavior + TLS passthrough details before I apply.
Sam Rivera: Current plan is to change service type and add annotations, example snippet I'm testing locally:
Sam Rivera: ```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  namespace: prod-inference
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-node-port: "32456"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
      nodePort: 32456
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
```
Sam Rivera: Questions: 1) healthcheck targetType should be `node`/instance or `ip`? 2) With `externalTrafficPolicy: Local` are we safe to rely on TLS passthrough (no LB termination)? 3) any secret wiring I should be careful of for gateway certs? @Tina
Tina Gomez: For NLB passthrough we usually use targetType=ip when the nodes aren't registering instance targets, but when using NodePort + externalTrafficPolicy: Local the NLB should hit node IPs (instance). TL;DR: use instance targetType if you want node healthchecks to match nodePort health.
Tina Gomez: If you want pure TCP passthrough (no LB TLS termination) set backend-protocol to tcp and don't attach cert to TG. Certs should remain on pods (k8s TLS secret mounted into pod). We'll want to ensure the service selector matches only ready pods on local nodes.
Ben Cho: Small gotcha — if you switch to NodePort and externalTrafficPolicy: Local, make sure `sessionAffinity` is `None` (default). Also confirm kube-proxy mode (ipvs vs iptables) but doesn't usually change targetType choice.
Ben Cho: For terraform side, the aws_lb_target_group resource will be created with `target_type = "instance"` if you're using instance-based registration. If you accidentally set target_type = "ip" but your nodes register as instance, healthchecks will fail.
Sam Rivera: Copy. Current cluster uses kube-proxy ipvs and nodes register as instances for k8s Service -> NLB integration.
Sam Rivera: InfraBot, can you run a quick preflight terraform plan for my branch? (pr: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/482)
InfraBot: preflight: running terraform plan against pr/482
InfraBot: plan summary:  ~1 to update,  +0 to add,  -0 to destroy
InfraBot: change: k8s_service.prod_inference.inference_gateway will be updated (type: ClusterIP -> NodePort ; annotations updated)
InfraBot: note: will assign nodePort 32456, externalTrafficPolicy -> Local
Tina Gomez: Also add this annotation so kube-controller registers targets as instance: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "instance"` — explicit is safer.
Tina Gomez: And double-check your health check path/port: NLB healthcheck will hit the nodePort (32456) over TCP, so your pods must respond on 8443 for the node to be healthy.
Layla Ortiz: Oncall note — if this hits prod, can we do a canary in staging+canary namespace first? Also add an automatic rollback plan in the PR description (how to revert service -> ClusterIP) :slightly_smiling_face:
Sam Rivera: Good call. I'll add a canary job and a terraform toggle in the PR (variable enable_nlb_passthrough = true). I'll also document how to revert.
Sam Rivera: Updated PR with annotation per Tina and canary variable; adding e2e smoke script that curls nodePort on one node.
Ben Cho: Ping me on the PR for a quick review; will check that secrets mounted into pod (k8s TLS secret) are unchanged and not referenced by LB.
InfraBot: plan re-run (post changes):  ~0 to update, +0 to add, -0 to destroy — ready to apply when approvals present
Sam Rivera: Thanks all. I'll wait for Ben + Tina approval then roll in canary window (10m) and monitor console metrics.
Tina Gomez: Sounds good. If anything weird, drop logs from `kubectl get endpoints -n prod-inference inference-gateway -o wide` and `kubectl describe svc`.
Sam Rivera: Will do. :thumbsup:
